def probe_wdl(self, board: chess.Board) -> int:
        """
        Probes WDL tables for win/draw/loss information under the 50-move rule,
        assuming the position has been reached directly after a capture or
        pawn move.

        Probing is thread-safe when done with different *board* objects and
        if *board* objects are not modified during probing.

        Returns ``2`` if the side to move is winning, ``0`` if the position is
        a draw and ``-2`` if the side to move is losing.

        Returns ``1`` in case of a cursed win and ``-1`` in case of a blessed
        loss. Mate can be forced but the position can be drawn due to the
        fifty-move rule.

        >>> import chess
        >>> import chess.syzygy
        >>>
        >>> with chess.syzygy.open_tablebase("data/syzygy/regular") as tablebase:
        ...     board = chess.Board("8/2K5/4B3/3N4/8/8/4k3/8 b - - 0 1")
        ...     print(tablebase.probe_wdl(board))
        ...
        -2

## Popeye Popeye is a free open-source cross-platform program for testing chess problems. It can be used for orthodox problems, but also supports a great deal of fairy chess elements (piece types, conditions and stipulations). Thanks to its "intelligent mode", Popeye is very fast at testing (almost) orthodox help and series (stale)mate problems. ## A bit of history Popeye was started in the 1980s by Philippe Schnoebelen in some Pascal dialect. It was later converted into C by Norbert Geissler. Development of most features has been done in C. ## Portability Popeye can be easily compiled using make and e.g. gcc for Linux and other Unix-oid operating systems. Depending on the availability of cross-compilers, executables for Windows and MacOS are provided for released versions. Popeye is known to have been compiled for other platforms, e.g. Android or WebAssembly. ## Companions - [Olive](https://github.com/dturevski/olive-gui) is a great cross-platform GUI for Popeye - [Teddy](https://problemskak.dk/download-Teddy.php) is a popular Windows GUI for Popeye - [FEN Tool](https://mutsuntsai.github.io/fen-tool/) allows using Popeye within the browser, both on mobile phones and regular computers - [Spinach] (experimental) speeds up Popeye by distributing its workload on different CPU cores - [Py2Web](https://www.yacpdb.org/#static/py2web) renders Popeye's output in web pages - [YACPDB](https://www.yacpdb.org/#static/home) Yet Another Chess Problem Database uses Py2Web to render solutions ## Awards In 2026, Popeye, as well as Dmitri Turevski (creator of Olive, Py2Web and YACPDB), is among the first recipients of a [WFCC](https://www.wfcc.ch/) Special Award.
